title: Two NHLBI pages print different adult sleep ranges, 7 to 9 and 7 to 8
summary: NHLBI's how-much-sleep page says adults should sleep 7 to 9 hours, while its sleep-deprivation table prints 7 to 8 hours for adults 18 and older.
body: The how-much-sleep page says experts recommend that adults sleep between 7 and 9 hours a night. It adds that less than 7 may go with more health issues than 7 or more, and that more than 9 is not necessarily harmful and may help young adults, people recovering from lost sleep, and people who are sick. The sleep-deprivation page's table, updated the same day, prints adults 18 or older as 7 to 8 hours a day, and it labels the 12-to-16-hour row as newborns 4 to 12 months rather than babies. This card does not pick a winner. Both lines are what those pages print. A child's range is the other card.
